name: Shit
lede: Shit is a dark olive-brown from an online color-name survey, a crowd's blunt name for a common brown that no color book defines.

sections.title: Where the name comes from
sections.body: The name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, in which respondents typed their own names for colors shown on screen [1]. It is not a traditional or industry color name, and no book among the color books we work from defines it as one [1]. The swatch is a moderate olive brown by ISCC-NBS, 6.6 units away [1]. We list it because people search for it, not because it has a history.

sections.title: What the books say about the thing
sections.body:
The books do talk about why this part of the color world is disliked. St Clair writes that brown is the color of earth, mud, filth and refuse, and suffers because it is a shade, not a hue: it has to be made by darkening and greying yellows, oranges and some reds, or by mixing the three artists' primaries [2]. See [[brown]], [[umber]] and [[camel]] for the respectable end of the family.

Painters also joke about it. Finlay writes that in art the shadows and the dirt are what make the light parts believable, an idea a conservator friend agreed with [3]. And the old stack process for lead white used dung in the making, a transformation Finlay calls shit into sugar [3]. Writers use the word for a color too, as when Maggie Nelson in *Bluets* describes a gym shower as baby-shit yellow, a different color from this swatch [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 321, 1.35 per cent, and is more common than 66 per cent of the named colors [5]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 0.8 per cent of 8,345 paintings, only 1.2 times the rate the same museums would predict, so it is no period color [5]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent (46 per cent of 149 works measured) [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [5].

questions.answer: It is a shade, not a hue

questions.q: True or false: Shit is a traditional pigment name.

openers: Brown is a shade made by greying yellows and oranges, which is why bright browns do not exist.

issues: Finlay's line about shadows making lights believable is her own, with a conservator agreeing; reattributed. All other claims (St Clair brown, stack process, Nelson Bluets) verified.
